answer: Each identity moors a vessel at one wharf berth, locking an 85-credit bond to its anchor chain. Its jade cargo weight and draft marks enter the berth log. An auditor recomputes displacement from the published table using weight and draft; a mismatch, reused chain serial, or copied reading burns the bond. First berthing costs 34; the kth berth of one funder costs 34+7(k-1), the 1000th 7027. 1000 fake berths pay 3,530,500 and lock 85,000, sharing no chain. A rented-berth ring fails: its chain serial sits in the log under another key. An honest operator pays 34 once and recovers the bond.
